Descriptive source: "វិធានការជីវសុវត្ថិភាព ដើម្បីបង្ការជំងឺផ្សាយបក្សី និងជំងឺបក្សីដទៃទៀត សៀវភៅណែនាំសំរាប់កសិកម្មចិញ្ចឹមបក្សីជាលក្ខណៈគ្រួសារ" (Biosecurity Measures to Prevent Avian Influenza and Other Poultry Diseases: A Guide for Household Poultry Raising), a joint FAO / USAID / MAFF publication produced under Cambodia-Germany cooperation, dated June 2009.
text:
Avian Influenza (AI, known locally as 'bird flu', ជំងឺផ្សាយបក្សី) is a poultry disease. The strain of concern here is highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), which can spread very quickly through a flock, kill birds within a short time, and also poses a risk to human health. Chickens, ducks, quail, and pigeons are all noted as susceptible, though ducks in particular can carry the virus (AIV) and shed it into the environment while showing no visible symptoms themselves - meaning an apparently healthy duck flock can still be a source of infection for other birds.

This source lists the main routes by which the virus spreads between farms and flocks:
1. Direct contact with sick birds or with poultry products (meat, eggs) that are carrying the virus.
2. Transporting sick birds or contaminated poultry products from one area to another.
3. Using vehicles, equipment, or materials that are contaminated with the virus.
4. Collecting/buying poultry from unclear or mixed sources across different locations.
5. Reusing other contaminated equipment or materials moved between different sites.
6. People entering areas close to poultry without appropriate precautions.
7. Free-ranging poultry kept without a secure coop or fencing, exposing them to contaminated water or environments shared with other birds.
8. Housing and roosting areas that are not cleaned and disinfected properly.
9. Indirect spread via rats, insects, flies, or free-flying wild birds such as sparrows and doves, in addition to people.
10. Feed or water drawn from unclean sources.
11. Housing different poultry species together without separation.

How this plays out in practice: this source illustrates a spread pattern where a farm sends poultry to market by motorbike or truck, using shared cages, holding baskets, and processing tools; the market brings together sellers, buyers, and birds from many different farms in one place; contaminated vehicles, equipment, or people (including footwear and clothing) then carry the virus onward to other farms. Wild or migratory birds visiting shared water sources, and unsafe disposal of dead birds (e.g., dumping them in a pond or waterway instead of burying them), are additional pathways highlighted in this source's diagram of how the virus circulates through a farm-market-farm cycle.

If a farmer suspects avian influenza in their flock, this source lists these numbers to call to report it: 012-833-795 or 012-264-970.
